issues.claim: "The current site also lays out at 980 px wide on a 390 px phone, so it appears shrunk instead of fitted" (audit_md), and "the browser scales it down at phone width" (domains[2].result).
issues.problem: The 980 px fixed layout is correct (document scrollWidth = 980 at every width). The "shrunk" appearance is supported by the saved screenshot nordlaw-mobile-390.png, which shows the whole desktop page fitted into 390 px. But when I re-ran it in this browser at a 390 px viewport (Chrome emulation, mobile, scale factor 3, navigation after emulation was set), the page kept its 980 px layout at visualViewport.scale = 1 and the right-hand content (nav, headline) was cut off rather than shrunk. So "shrunk to fit" is device-dependent: some phones show a tiny full-width page, others show a cut-off page. The audit states one of the two behaviours as fact.
issues.fix: Say "the page keeps its 980-pixel desktop layout on a phone, so it is scaled down to tiny text on some phones and cut off on others, instead of fitting the screen" - and keep the phone screenshot as the example of one case.

issues.claim: founder_md outreach draft: "Your current site at nordlaw.legal and your Google profile are fine, so the loose end is the old domain plus the listings that still point at it."
issues.problem: Plural "listings" implies more than one place still links the old domain. I could only find one: the Lawyers.com East Brunswick profile. The Martindale profile shows no website field, the Lawyers.com Toms River profile (228 Main Street) carries no external link, and the firm's own site links nothing to nord-demaio.com. audit_md correctly says "One directory".
issues.fix: Change to "the Lawyers.com profile that still points at it" so the email matches audit_md and is exactly true.

issues.claim: audit_md: "the site cites nearly 40 years of practice".
issues.problem: The site's own words are "a wealth of nearly 40 years' experience navigating... the law", which is experience rather than 40 years of the firm's practice. Close, but the audit's paraphrase says slightly more than the source does.
issues.fix: Quote it as the site does: "cites nearly 40 years' experience".
